fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Pre-Training Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey, its scoring, and the table behind it. A follow-up prompt changes any part before learners are invited.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from your course outline

Paste the course outline or the skills the session covers. Emergent drafts knowledge, confidence and logistics questions for it, and a follow-up prompt rewords or cuts any one.
fields.feature_2:
A pre-test scored against your answer key

Mark the right option for each knowledge question. The app scores every pre-test on submit and counts how many learners missed each question, so the trainer knows where to start.
fields.feature_3:
Session placement by score or role

Set a score cutoff or a role filter, and the app assigns each learner a session or track. The rule lives in the survey logic, and a prompt moves the cutoff before invitations go out.
fields.feature_4:
A baseline kept for the after-survey

Every answer is a row in a database you own, tagged with the learner and the course. Send the same questions after training and put both scores side by side for each person.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders before the session starts

Learners who have not answered get an email reminder 2 days before the session. The trainer gets a Slack message listing who is still out, and anyone finished gets no more emails.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and your code on paid plans

Host the survey on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and reuse it for each cohort.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Teams Survey Before Training
fields.tab_content_1:
Rebooking leads day one after 29 of 35 miss it

A week before Ravelstoke Freight trains 38 dispatchers on new dispatch software, each takes an 8-question pre-test, and 35 answered. Rebooking a missed pickup was wrong on 29 of 35 tests. Route changes, the next-hardest, was missed 11 times. The trainer moved rebooking into the first hour of day one.
fields.tab_content_2:
Advanced seats go to anyone with 4 of 5 right

Quillfirth Accounting runs one training week for 56 staff, with advanced and foundations sessions. Before it starts, everyone gets 5 spreadsheet questions, and 52 answer. Anyone with 4 or more right is emailed an advanced seat; the rest get foundations. The split came out at 21 advanced and 31 foundations.
fields.tab_content_3:
Hard conversations lead with 22 votes from 36

Larchwell Grocers promoted 40 store managers this year. Before their leadership workshop, each picks one skill for the day to cover, and 36 answered. Hard conversations with staff took 22 votes, with shift scheduling next at 9. The trainer made the afternoon role-play on those conversations.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any access need emails the coordinator

Five days before onboarding week, Tavistry Software asks its 18 new hires for their time zone, their laptop setup, and any access needs. An answer in the access field sends the training coordinator an email with a link to it. Two hires asked for live captions, and both were booked before day one.

fields.howto_title: How to Run a Pre-Training Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write pre training survey questions that set each learner's baseline and change the plan before day one.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Pair each skill with a confidence rating
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask what the learner wants covered
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the tasks a learner should be able to do after training, in the words the job uses. Each task becomes one or two pre-test questions. Paste that list into your prompt, and Emergent drafts the questions from it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Build each knowledge question around a real moment on the job, such as rebooking a missed pickup. Give it one right option and a not-sure-yet option. A lucky guess then never counts as knowledge.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask learners to rate their confidence in each skill from 1 to 5. A low score beside high confidence marks a topic to correct early. A high score beside low confidence points to someone who needs practice more than new content.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add one question on what the learner wants the day to cover and one on access needs, like captions or a seat near the screen. Keep the whole survey to 10 questions or fewer, about 5 minutes of a learner's time.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Send it about a week out
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the survey 5 to 7 days before training. A week leaves time to move a topic into the first hour or open a second session. Set the deadline for the day before training, and give the trainer that evening to read the results.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Say the score is not a grade
fields.howto_step_6_des: Tell learners in the invitation that the pre-test sets their starting point and nobody is graded on it. Ask them to answer without looking anything up. A baseline built from searched answers hides the gaps the training is meant to close.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Keep the wording for the after-survey
fields.howto_step_7_des: After training, send the knowledge questions again with the same wording and the same answer options. A reworded question breaks the comparison for that question. Keep the set fixed across cohorts too, and this year's gains sit beside next year's.

faq_plan.q: What are pre training survey questions?
How do I create pre training survey questions?

plan.angle: The top 10 for pre training survey questions are question lists and templates (TalentLMS, SmartSurvey, RapidoForm, HeySurvey, Pointerpro) that stop at the wording, and half of them are about post-training feedback. This page stays before the session: it shows four pre training surveys built from a prompt that set a baseline score, place learners into the right session, shape the agenda from what learners ask for, and catch access needs before day one, with every answer saved so the same questions can be asked again after training. The how-to covers timing, length, scoring and what to do with the answers; the FAQ covers wording, timing, anonymity, length and reuse.
tab_stories: Ravelstoke Freight sends an 8-question pre-test to 38 dispatchers a week before training on new dispatch software, 35 answer, 29 of 35 miss the question on rebooking a missed pickup, and the trainer moves that topic into the first hour.

Quillfirth Accounting asks 56 staff 5 spreadsheet questions before its training week, 52 answer, anyone with 4 or more right is emailed a seat in the advanced session, and the split is 21 advanced and 31 foundations.

Larchwell Grocers asks its 40 new store managers what they most want to handle better before a leadership workshop, 36 answer, 22 pick hard conversations with staff, and the trainer turns the afternoon into role-play on those conversations.

Tavistry Software asks 18 new hires about time zone, laptop setup and access needs before onboarding week, any access need emails the training coordinator, and 2 caption requests are booked before day one.
